blind_spots.blind_spot: A general-aviation qualification envelope on hardware being pulled toward military platforms
blind_spots.operator_reality: The published PDAS envelope stops at +50C and -10C. A box that flies on an Air Force test aircraft or a fielded UAS gets asked for DO-160 or MIL-STD-810 across roughly -40 to +71C plus altitude, humidity, vibration, shock and salt fog, and MIL-STD-461 for conducted and radiated emissions. Qualification testing is not a firmware sprint — it is chamber time, lab scheduling, failures, redesign and re-test, typically six to twelve months and a six-figure line item. For a three-person company, discovering that requirement after the contract is signed is precisely the case where months-to-field exceeds funded months remaining.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial customer base is student pilots, flight schools and a test pilot school flying benign profiles from improved fields, where nobody has ever asked for an environmental qualification report.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Maximum Ratings: Acceleration: +/- 16 g; Rotation: +/- 2,000 deg/s; Airspeed: 0 to 340 knots; Altitude: -10,000 to +70,000 ft; Temperature: -10 to +50C

blind_spots.blind_spot: The default flight-data workflow runs through consumer cloud services and an unmanaged tablet
blind_spots.operator_reality: Flight test data from a military platform — control law responses, flying qualities, performance points — is CUI at minimum and frequently program-protected. Their shipping workflow streams GDL90 over Wi-Fi to ForeFlight on someone's iPad and uploads logs to third-party cloud analysis services. On a military test program that is both a spillage path and an RF emissions issue, and the test engineer will default to the documented workflow unless an offline, air-gap-friendly path exists and is the one in the manual. The fix is cheap now (local export, no-RF mode, documented handling) and expensive after an incident report.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Cloud sharing is a genuine selling point to flight schools and researchers, so it was engineered as the primary path rather than an optional one.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Real-time streaming: GDL90 output to apps like ForeFlight for GPS and backup AHRS ... Connectivity: Bluetooth + Wi-Fi

blind_spots.blind_spot: Building UAS flight control hardware with no visible export-control function
blind_spots.operator_reality: A fault-tolerant flight control system and autopilot for unmanned aircraft is squarely the kind of technical data that lands on the USML, and the obligations attach to the drawings, source and test data — not just to shipping a box overseas. This is a three-person company that co-developed PDAS with the International Test Pilots School and just announced a co-development partnership for U.S.-manufactured UAS autopilots. Registration, an empowered official, technical-data segregation and deemed-export controls on any non-US person touching the repo are all company-level work that has to exist before a Phase III or a prime subcontract can flow down to them, and it is the kind of finding that stops an award rather than delaying it.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: 'Manufactured in the USA' is treated on the site as a marketing attribute and a supply-chain claim, which reads as if the export question is already answered.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Manufactured in the USA: designed, manufactured, and assembled in the U.S., with U.S. sourced materials wherever possible

opener_hook: Your PDAS spec sheet publishes a maximum temperature rating of -10 to +50C, which is a general-aviation envelope, while FA930225C0008 with Air Force Test Center points that same hardware at platforms whose qualification baseline starts around -40C and MIL-STD-461.
